title: Indoor Unit Room Temperature Sensor Error
shortDescription: Samsung mini-split detects a fault in the indoor room temperature sensor circuit.
fullDescription:
The E1 error on Samsung mini-split systems indicates an open or short circuit in the indoor room temperature thermistor. The unit cannot accurately measure ambient room temperature and will typically shut down to protect components.

Common causes include a loose sensor plug on the main PCB, a failed thermistor, or moisture intrusion. Once the sensor is replaced or the connection restored, the error clears automatically after a successful restart.
safetyWarning: Disconnect power at the breaker before opening the indoor unit cover.

causes.cause: Disconnected or loose thermistor connector on indoor PCB

fixSteps.title: Power off the unit
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off the breaker feeding the mini-split.

fixSteps.title: Open indoor front panel
fixSteps.instruction: Lift the front cover and remove the electrical box cover screws.

fixSteps.title: Reseat thermistor plug
fixSteps.instruction: Locate the small 2-pin thermistor connector on the PCB (usually labeled ROOM) and reseat firmly.

fixSteps.title: Test resistance
fixSteps.instruction: With unit powered off, measure thermistor resistance - should be about 10k ohms at 25C.

whenToCallPro: Call an HVAC pro if the PCB itself is defective or if you are uncomfortable working inside the indoor unit.

faq.q: Can I keep running the unit with E1?
faq.a: No, the unit will not regulate temperature properly and may cycle off.

title: Indoor Coil (Evaporator) Sensor Error
shortDescription: Evaporator coil temperature sensor is open, shorted, or out of range.
fullDescription:
E2 indicates the indoor coil thermistor has failed or become disconnected. This sensor is essential for defrost logic and anti-freeze protection.

The unit will stop cooling/heating to prevent icing or overheating of the evaporator. Replacing the sensor or reseating its connector typically resolves the fault.

fixSteps.title: Access coil sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove front grille and follow thin white/black sensor wire to the evaporator coil clip.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Clip a new thermistor onto the same spot on the coil and route wiring back to the PCB.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the sensor is integrated into the coil assembly.

faq.a: No - the unit shuts down to prevent damage.

title: Indoor Fan Motor Error
shortDescription: Indoor blower fan motor speed feedback is out of range or missing.
fullDescription:
E3 means the indoor fan motor is not turning at the commanded speed, or the PCB is not receiving the tachometer feedback signal. Causes range from a stuck fan wheel to a failed DC fan motor.

On BLDC-equipped Samsung units the motor and PCB must be compatible; mismatched parts can trigger this fault even after replacement.
safetyWarning: DC fan motors retain voltage briefly - wait 5 minutes after disconnecting power.

fixSteps.title: Power off
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect at breaker and wait 5 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Inspect fan wheel
fixSteps.instruction: Spin by hand to check for obstructions or stiff bearings.

fixSteps.title: Test motor
fixSteps.instruction: If bearings are stiff or motor does not respond on power, replace fan motor assembly.

whenToCallPro: Call an HVAC pro if the motor replacement requires removing the blower wheel or evaporator coil.

faq.q: Can I use any generic fan motor?
faq.a: No, BLDC motors must match Samsung's PCB control signals.

title: EEPROM / Memory Error
shortDescription: The indoor unit's PCB cannot read configuration data from EEPROM.
fullDescription:
E4 is reported when the PCB's non-volatile memory returns bad data or cannot be read. Without valid EEPROM data the unit does not know its model characteristics and refuses to run.

This typically requires PCB replacement, though a power cycle sometimes clears a transient fault.

fixSteps.title: Hard power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Cut breaker for 10 minutes, then restore.

fixSteps.title: Replace PCB
fixSteps.instruction: If fault returns, replace indoor PCB with a model-specific board.

whenToCallPro: PCB replacement and reprogramming should be done by a licensed HVAC technician.

faq.a: No, Samsung indoor PCBs are model-specific.

title: Indoor-Outdoor Communication Error
shortDescription: The indoor unit cannot communicate with the outdoor unit over the S-bus.
fullDescription:
E5 indicates loss of the communication signal between indoor and outdoor units. Samsung mini-splits use a 3-wire interconnect (L, N, S) where the S wire carries data.

Common issues include miswired S/N terminals, damaged interconnect cable, or a failed outdoor inverter PCB.
safetyWarning: Line voltage is present on the interconnect - shut off power before inspection.

fixSteps.title: Verify outdoor power
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm outdoor breaker and disconnect are on.

fixSteps.title: Check terminal wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Match terminals 1-1, 2-2, 3-3 between indoor and outdoor units.

fixSteps.title: Measure S-wire voltage
fixSteps.instruction: With unit on, expect pulsing 30-80 VDC between S and N. Zero suggests open wire or dead PCB.

whenToCallPro: If voltage on S wire is missing and outdoor has power, the outdoor PCB likely needs replacement.

faq.q: Is the S wire low voltage?
faq.a: No - it carries up to ~100V pulses referenced to N.

title: Communication Error (Newer Models)
shortDescription: Extended code equivalent to E5 on newer Samsung units - indoor-outdoor communication lost.
fullDescription:
E101 is the detailed diagnostic code on Samsung's newer 4-digit display units for communication failure between indoor and outdoor. The troubleshooting path mirrors E5.

It often appears after storms or when an outdoor breaker has tripped.

fixSteps.title: Reset breakers
fixSteps.instruction: Cycle both indoor and outdoor breakers off for 5 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Inspect interconnect
fixSteps.instruction: Look for pinched or burned spots in the line-set wiring chase.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro when cable replacement or PCB diagnostics are required.

faq.q: Is E101 the same as E5?
faq.a: Yes, on newer models with 4-digit displays.

title: Indoor-Outdoor Communication Tracking Error
shortDescription: Outdoor unit cannot match addresses with the indoor unit.
fullDescription:
E102 appears when the outdoor unit initially pairs with the indoor unit but loses synchronization. This can be caused by electrical noise on the S-bus, a failing inverter PCB, or a recently replaced indoor/outdoor pair that was not re-addressed.

On multi-split systems, conflicting indoor addresses can also cause E102.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle all units
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off all indoor and outdoor breakers for 10 minutes and restore simultaneously.

fixSteps.title: Check DIP switches
fixSteps.instruction: On multi-splits, ensure each indoor unit has a unique address.

whenToCallPro: Multi-split readdressing and PCB diagnostics should be performed by an HVAC technician.

faq.a: Only if the issue is address conflict; otherwise the outdoor PCB is the likely cause.

title: Main-Sub Indoor Communication Error
shortDescription: Main indoor PCB cannot communicate with display/remote PCB.
fullDescription:
E103 indicates a fault between the main indoor PCB and the display PCB that holds the IR receiver. Often caused by a dislodged ribbon cable after servicing.

Check the small ribbon connector between the display board behind the front panel and the main PCB in the electrical box.
symptoms: Display works but unit does not respond

fixSteps.title: Reseat ribbon cable
fixSteps.instruction: Open front panel and reseat the flex/ribbon connector at both ends.

whenToCallPro: If reseating doesn't help, a technician will need to replace the display or main PCB.

faq.a: Yes - commands from remote cannot reach the main PCB.

title: Indoor Fan Locked / Overcurrent
shortDescription: Indoor fan draws too much current or is locked.
fullDescription:
E201 is triggered when the indoor fan motor is stalled or drawing excessive current. Typical causes are debris in the blower wheel, foreign objects, or a failing motor bearing.

Correct by removing the obstruction or replacing the motor. Persistent E201 after motor replacement suggests PCB drive circuit failure.

fixSteps.title: Inspect fan
fixSteps.instruction: Remove front panel and spin blower wheel by hand.

fixSteps.title: Clean or replace
fixSteps.instruction: Clean wheel; if bearings are stiff, replace motor.

whenToCallPro: Motor replacement requiring blower wheel removal is best left to a pro.

faq.q: Can I just oil the motor?
faq.a: No - Samsung indoor fans use sealed bearings.

title: Indoor Fan No Feedback
shortDescription: Indoor fan runs but no tach signal returns to the PCB.
fullDescription:
E202 is tripped when the indoor fan lacks feedback (Hall sensor) signal, even though the drive output appears correct. The motor will keep running but the PCB cannot confirm speed and shuts down after ~30 seconds.

Commonly caused by a bad motor Hall sensor inside the fan or a broken yellow feedback wire.

causes.cause: Broken Hall sensor wire in motor harness

fixSteps.title: Inspect harness
fixSteps.instruction: Check for broken wires in the motor harness at the connector crimps.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor
fixSteps.instruction: If harness is intact but feedback wire has no pulse on startup, replace motor.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro for motor replacement.

faq.a: No, but the unit will not run.

title: Outdoor Pipe Temperature Sensor Error
shortDescription: Outdoor discharge pipe or condenser coil sensor failure.
fullDescription:
E301 reports a fault on the outdoor unit's refrigerant pipe temperature sensor. Without this reading, the inverter cannot modulate compressor speed safely and shuts down.

Access requires removing the outdoor service panel. Replacement sensors are inexpensive but require careful routing away from hot components.
safetyWarning: The outdoor unit has high voltage capacitors - wait 10 minutes after power off.

fixSteps.title: Open outdoor top cover
fixSteps.instruction: Remove top cover screws to access sensors on the coil and discharge pipe.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Unclip old sensor, install new one in same spot, re-route wiring.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if sensor replacement requires opening the refrigerant circuit (it usually does not).

faq.a: Usually the 2-wire thermistor clipped to the condenser inlet pipe.

title: Compressor Startup Failure
shortDescription: Compressor fails to start or loses rotor lock during startup.
fullDescription:
E401 is an inverter compressor start failure. Samsung inverter compressors need precise rotor alignment at startup; if the inverter detects back-EMF mismatch it aborts and reports E401.

Causes include low refrigerant (pressure equalization issue), IPM module weakness, or compressor winding faults.
safetyWarning: High voltage DC is present on inverter - only qualified techs should probe live.

causes.cause: Low refrigerant charge causing high starting pressure

fixSteps.title: Hard reset
fixSteps.instruction: Cut power for 10 minutes and retry.

fixSteps.title: Call technician
fixSteps.instruction: If fault persists, a tech must measure inverter output and compressor winding resistance.

whenToCallPro: Always - this involves inverter, refrigerant, and compressor diagnostics.

faq.a: Not always - often it's the IPM module that fails first.

title: High Pressure Switch Trip
shortDescription: The outdoor high pressure switch has opened, indicating excessive discharge pressure.
fullDescription:
E402 signals that the high pressure safety switch has opened. This normally protects the compressor from excessive condensing pressure, often due to a dirty outdoor coil, failed outdoor fan, or restricted airflow in heating mode.

In heating, a dirty indoor filter or blocked blower can also cause this.
safetyWarning: Do not bypass the pressure switch - it prevents compressor rupture.

causes.cause: Indoor filter or coil blocked (in heating)

fixSteps.title: Wash condenser coil
fixSteps.instruction: Spray outdoor fins with a gentle hose from inside out.

fixSteps.title: Verify outdoor fan
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure outdoor fan runs whenever compressor runs in cooling.

fixSteps.title: Clean indoor filter
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and wash the indoor air filter.

whenToCallPro: If airflow is fine and fault returns, a tech must check charge and pressures.

faq.a: It auto-resets, but you must fix the root cause.

title: Inverter IPM (Power Module) Over-current
shortDescription: The outdoor inverter IPM detected an over-current during compressor operation.
fullDescription:
E464 is thrown when the intelligent power module (IPM) in the outdoor inverter detects a current spike to the compressor. This can be from a shorted compressor winding, low voltage supply, or a failing IPM.

It is one of the more serious Samsung faults and usually requires outdoor PCB or compressor replacement.
safetyWarning: Lethal DC voltages present in the inverter after power-off. Wait 10 minutes minimum.

fixSteps.title: Check supply voltage
fixSteps.instruction: Measure voltage at outdoor disconnect - should be within 10% of rated.

fixSteps.title: Tech diagnostic
fixSteps.instruction: Have a pro measure compressor winding resistance (should be balanced) and inspect IPM.

whenToCallPro: Always call a licensed HVAC technician.

faq.a: On units over 10 years old, often no - weigh repair cost against new system.

title: Outdoor Temperature Sensor Error
shortDescription: Ambient outdoor temperature sensor is open or shorted.
fullDescription:
E500 refers to the outdoor ambient thermistor failure. This sensor is used for defrost initiation and compressor speed modulation.

Like other Samsung thermistors, nominal resistance is ~10k ohms at 25C. Replacement is straightforward for an experienced DIYer with the outdoor cover removed.

fixSteps.title: Locate sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Ambient thermistor hangs freely near the coil inlet - reseat connector.

fixSteps.title: Replace if needed
fixSteps.instruction: If resistance is infinite or zero, replace with matching thermistor.

whenToCallPro: Only if you are uncomfortable working in the outdoor electrical box.

faq.a: Sometimes limited cooling operates but defrost in heating will be impaired.

title: Communication Address Duplication
shortDescription: Two indoor units share the same address.
fullDescription: More than one indoor unit on a multi-zone has the same identifier; the controller cannot route commands correctly.
safetyWarning: Turn off power at the breaker before opening the unit. HVAC systems contain high-voltage components and refrigerant under pressure.

causes.cause: Loose wiring or connector at terminal block
Sensor or thermistor out of calibration

symptoms: E108 shown on display or remote
Unit will not start or shuts down quickly
Indoor or outdoor fan behavior abnormal

fixSteps.title: Power Reset
fixSteps.instruction: Switch off the breaker for 5 minutes, then restore power and observe whether the code returns.

fixSteps.title: Visual Inspection
fixSteps.instruction: With power off, open the service panel and inspect connectors, sensor leads, and contactors for damage or looseness.

fixSteps.title: Call Technician
fixSteps.instruction: If the fault persists after a reset and visual check, contact a licensed HVAC technician for component-level diagnosis.

repairTime: 30 minutes to 3 hours depending on root cause
whenToCallPro: Call a licensed HVAC technician if a power reset and basic inspection do not clear the fault, or any time refrigerant or sealed-system work is required.

faq.a: Only the power reset and visual checks are DIY-safe; component diagnosis or refrigerant work requires a licensed technician.
Typical service calls run $150-$500; sealed-system or compressor work can exceed $1,500.
If the unit is not heating or cooling at all, treat it as urgent. If it self-recovers, schedule service soon to prevent recurrence.

fixSteps.instruction: With power off, open the service panel and inspect connectors, sensor leads, and contactors for damage or looseness.

fixSteps.title: Call Technician
fixSteps.instruction: If the fault persists after a reset and visual check, contact a licensed HVAC technician for component-level diagnosis.

repairTime: 30 minutes to 3 hours depending on root cause
whenToCallPro: Call a licensed HVAC technician if a power reset and basic inspection do not clear the fault, or any time refrigerant or sealed-system work is required.

faq.a: Only the power reset and visual checks are DIY-safe; component diagnosis or refrigerant work requires a licensed technician.
Typical service calls run $150-$500; sealed-system or compressor work can exceed $1,500.
If the unit is not heating or cooling at all, treat it as urgent. If it self-recovers, schedule service soon to prevent recurrence.

title: Outdoor Communication Polarity
shortDescription: Communication wires between indoor and outdoor have reversed polarity.
fullDescription: Samsung E450 indicates the F1/F2 or comms polarity is swapped, preventing proper handshake.

fixSteps.title: Check polarity
fixSteps.instruction: Verify F1/F2 match between indoor and outdoor terminals.

faq.a: Yes — most common after a new install.

safetyWarning: De-energize before working on terminal blocks.

title: Indoor BLDC Fan Lock
shortDescription: Indoor BLDC blower motor is locked.
fullDescription: E451 indicates the brushless indoor blower motor cannot rotate — debris, bearing failure, or driver issue.

fixSteps.title: Power off, rotate by hand
fixSteps.instruction: Spin the wheel and check for binding.

whenToCallPro: If driver replacement on PCB needed.

faq.a: Higher than AC motors but more efficient.

title: Indoor Display PCB Lost
shortDescription: Indoor display board lost communication with main board.
fullDescription: E452 indicates loss of comms between the indoor display and the main control PCB.

fixSteps.title: Reseat ribbon
fixSteps.instruction: Open the front panel and reseat the display ribbon cable.

fixSteps.title: Replace display
fixSteps.instruction: Swap display board if reseat fails.

faq.a: Sometimes — IR remote may still work.

title: Outdoor Heat Sink Overheat
shortDescription: Outdoor inverter heatsink temperature exceeded limit.
fullDescription: E453 indicates the inverter heatsink overheated, often from a failed or restricted outdoor fan.

fixSteps.title: Clean heatsink
fixSteps.instruction: Brush dust off the inverter heatsink fins.

whenToCallPro: If fan motor or PCB needs work.

title: Compressor Discharge Sensor Open
shortDescription: Discharge pipe thermistor is open circuit.
fullDescription: E454 indicates the compressor discharge sensor is reading open, removing high-temp protection.

fixSteps.title: Inspect wire
fixSteps.instruction: Check for heat damage near compressor.

fixSteps.title: Replace
fixSteps.instruction: Install OEM thermistor with heat sleeve.

whenToCallPro: If sensor location is hard to reach.
safetyWarning: Compressor extremely hot during operation.

title: Outdoor Suction Sensor Short
fullDescription: E455 indicates the suction line thermistor at the outdoor unit reads shorted, preventing superheat control.

fixSteps.title: Inspect wire
fixSteps.instruction: Look for pinches near pipe insulation.

faq.a: May cycle but performance is poor.

title: Outdoor EEV Coil Fault
shortDescription: Electronic expansion valve coil is open.
fullDescription: E456 indicates the EEV coil winding is open, preventing flow modulation.

fixSteps.title: Replace coil
fixSteps.instruction: Slip new coil over valve body.

faq.a: Different fault — E466 was high-pressure-related on this brand.

title: Power Module Over Current Soft
fullDescription: E457 indicates the inverter saw a brief but repeated over-current that triggered protection.

faq.a: Yes — soft trips are early warnings.

safetyWarning: Inverter retains lethal DC voltage.

title: Outdoor PCB Watchdog Reset
shortDescription: Outdoor PCB watchdog timer reset the controller.
fullDescription: E458 indicates the outdoor PCB firmware hung and the watchdog forced a reset.

fixSteps.title: Firmware update
fixSteps.instruction: Service tech updates firmware via service tool.

fixSteps.title: Replace PCB
fixSteps.instruction: If firmware does not fix, swap PCB.

title: Mode Conflict Multi-Zone
shortDescription: Two or more zones called for opposing modes simultaneously.
fullDescription: E459 (multi-zone units) indicates one zone is calling for cool while another calls for heat — system cannot satisfy both.

fixSteps.title: Set all zones same mode
fixSteps.instruction: Choose all heat or all cool from each remote.

whenToCallPro: If users cannot follow the mode-lock pattern.

faq.a: No — it is a multi-zone limitation of single-circuit systems.
